title: Network supply (A1-A6)
description: Road graph, signal control, transit supply, light rail vehicle and dwell, parking and the active network. Two of the three inputs the proposal named as critical and unobtained live here - A.signals.scats_phasing and A.lightrail.dwell_charging_s - and both carry status 'unobtained' with a null value, so the resolver refuses to hand back a point value and the caller must select a sweep member. That is DECISIONS.md 0 and 13 enforced structurally rather than by discipline.

A.road.lanes_default.sweep_basis: the plausible range for an unlabelled edge of each class
A.road.lanes_default.description: Fallback lane count where OSM carries no lanes tag. Applied only to edges with no observation - DECISIONS.md 2.5 corrected the proposal premise that the corridor is 75-98% imputed: as-built trunk lane counts are observed in OSM for 87.5% of corridor trunk edges. Full class table is in the build script; the registry overrides per class.

A.road.speed_default.description: Fallback free-flow speed where OSM carries no maxspeed tag.

A.road.capacity_default.description: Saturation flow by road class. Never observed; a class-level convention.

A.corridor.trunk_buffer_m.description: Distance from the alignment within which a road edge is classified corridor trunk.

A.corridor.cross_buffer_m.description: Distance within which a turn restriction or cross street is treated as on the corridor. At 40 m, 10 of the 1,385 resolved restrictions fall on the alignment, against the 14 E1 assumed.

A.corridor.parallel_buffer_m.description: Distance within which a road is treated as a parallel route that may absorb diverted traffic.

A.corridor.pre_lr_lanes_per_dir.sweep_basis: both values are plausible from the historical record; neither is observed
A.corridor.pre_lr_lanes_per_dir.description: Hunter/Scott cross-section BEFORE the light rail. THIS IS THE COUNTERFACTUAL HYPOTHESIS B3 RESTS ON and it is assumed, not observed. It must be reported as swept and never as a point estimate.

A.corridor.extension_lane_take.description: Lanes removed per direction where an S4/S5 extension runs in the carriageway.

A.corridor.off_corridor_penalty.description: Routing penalty that keeps a reconstructed alignment on observed geometry.

sweep.basis: proposal 7.2 fallback: infer effective signal delay from GTFS-Realtime run-time distributions and treat cycle time and priority as SWEPT parameters rather than fixed inputs

A.signals.scats_phasing.description: SCATS phase data for the Hunter/Scott corridor. NOT OBTAINED - a formal TfNSW request is outstanding. It determines corridor run time more than any other single input: the swing between no priority and full priority is 38% (S2 vs S2b). Every program in the SUMO corridor is labelled timing_source=assumed. THIS FIELD HAS NO POINT VALUE AND THE RESOLVER WILL NOT INVENT ONE: select a sweep member explicitly.

A.signals.delay_per_intersection_s.description: Proxy signal delay per corridor intersection, used to decompose scheduled run time in the absence of SCATS phasing. Downstream of A.signals.scats_phasing.

A.signals.n_corridor_intersections.description: Signalised intersections on the corridor. All 14 match a signalised junction in every SUMO road variant and every realised cycle lands within 1 s of its A2 value.

A.signals.min_green_s.description: Minimum green time in a generated SUMO signal program.

A.signals.junction_match_m.description: Radius for matching an A2 intersection to a SUMO junction.

A.lightrail.dwell_charging_s.sweep_basis: DECISIONS.md 4.3; the shipped scenario descriptions use 20 s as the baseline sweep point, which lives in the scenario config, not on this field
A.lightrail.dwell_charging_s.description: Supercapacitor charging dwell added at each intermediate stop. NOT MEASURED - a few hours of field observation at Civic or Crown Street would resolve it (DECISIONS.md 13 priority 2). Worth about 11% of end-to-end run time, and it is the subject of secondary question S-a: the marginal cost of the wire-free decision, taken with a late 35m urban amenity package. Modelled as a SEPARATE ADDITIVE TERM so it can be toggled independently of boarding dwell (S2 vs S2a). THIS FIELD HAS NO POINT VALUE.

A.lightrail.dwell_fixed_s.description: Boarding and alighting dwell, separate from charging dwell.

A.lightrail.capacity_total.description: Maximum capacity of the CAF Urbos 100 as published, and the figure DECISIONS.md 4.1 records. The mapped fleet carried 180 seats with no standing room, which is pt2matsim generic tram default and reconciles with neither the published maximum nor the assumed seated figure (issue 18).

sweep.basis: The seated/standing split of the Urbos 100 is NOT published; only the 270 maximum is. 60 is the class-typical figure already recorded in DECISIONS.md 4.1 for a 33 m five-module 100% low-floor LRV, and the interval spans the seating layouts that class carries. Swept because it is assumed, never pinned.

A.lightrail.capacity_seated.description: Seats on a light rail vehicle. Only the split is assumed - the total it is taken from is observed.

A.lightrail.capacity_standing.description: Standing room on a light rail vehicle. Not a free value: it is whatever the published maximum leaves once seats are taken out. Before this existed, no vehicle in the fleet had standing room at all, so the C1 crowding multipliers could never apply in any scenario (issue 18).

sweep.basis: the two Volvo models Newcastle actually runs: B12BLE 44 seated, B10B 51 seated (DECISIONS.md 9.21). Not a chosen interval - it is the observed spread of the fleet in service.

A.transit.bus_capacity_seated.description: Seats on a Newcastle bus. Published Volvo B12BLE figure. The mapped fleet carried pt2matsim's generic 70 seats, overstating seats by about 59% (issue 18).

sweep.basis: the published B12BLE standing figure plus or minus the usual crush-load tolerance; standing capacity is a rating, not a count, and no Newcastle-specific figure exists.

A.transit.bus_capacity_standing.description: Standing room on a Newcastle bus. Published B12BLE figure, 44 + 18 = 62 total. Before issue 18 NO vehicle in the fleet had standing room, so the C1 crowding multipliers were inert by construction.

held_fixed.rule: A published vessel capacity is a fact about the boat, not a behavioural parameter, and sweeping it would assert an uncertainty that does not exist. Both Stockton ferries carry the same published figure.
held_fixed.departure_requires: a different vessel entering service on the Stockton route

A.transit.ferry_capacity_total.description: Published capacity of the Stockton ferries MV Shortland and MV Hunter. The mapped fleet carried 250 seats and no standing room, overstating by 25%.

held_fixed.rule: Published seated capacity, held on the same reasoning as the total: it is a fact about the vessel. This is the ONLY vehicle in the fleet whose seated/standing split is published - tram and rail both have an assumed, swept seated share because only their totals are.
held_fixed.departure_requires: a different vessel entering service on the Stockton route

A.transit.ferry_capacity_seated.description: Published seated capacity of the Stockton ferries. Unlike rail and light rail, the ferry split IS published, so neither half is assumed.

A.transit.ferry_capacity_standing.description: Standing room on a Stockton ferry. Whatever the published total leaves once the published seats are taken out - both halves are published, so this identity carries no assumption.

sweep.basis: the two railcar classes on the Hunter Line: a two-car Hunter set is 77 (HM) + 69 (HMT) = 146, a two-car Endeavour set 95 (LE) + 82 (TE) = 177 (DECISIONS.md 9.21). The interval is the observed spread of stock in service, not a chosen range.

A.transit.rail_capacity_total.description: Capacity of a two-car Hunter Line set. The mapped fleet carried pt2matsim's generic 400 seats with no standing room - overstating a two-car set by roughly 2.7x, which is part of why transit capacity never binds (DECISIONS.md 9.12, issue 18).

sweep.basis: the seated/standing split of the Hunter and Endeavour railcars is NOT published; only the per-car capacity is. 98 is two thirds of the 146 total, the class-typical proportion for a regional railcar with vestibules, and the interval spans the layouts that class carries. Swept because it is assumed, never pinned.

A.transit.rail_capacity_seated.description: Seats on a two-car Hunter Line set. Only the SPLIT is assumed - the total it comes from is published.

A.transit.rail_capacity_standing.description: Standing room on a two-car Hunter Line set. Not a free value: whatever the published total leaves once seats are taken out.

A.lightrail.line_speed_kmh.description: Light rail running speed between stops, used in the run-time decomposition.

A.lightrail.corridor_speed_kmh.description: Design speed on the reserved corridor sections.

sweep.basis: S2 runs without priority, S2b with full priority - the 38% swing

A.lightrail.tsp_enabled.description: Transit signal priority on the corridor. Downstream of A.signals.scats_phasing.

A.transit.interchange_radius_m.description: Radius within which two stops are treated as one interchange for transfer generation.

A.transit.walk_speed_ms.description: Walk speed used to generate GTFS transfer times. Distinct from the MATSim teleported walk speed - see RUN.matsim.teleported_walk_speed_ms, which is 1.05.

A.transit.era1_line_speed_kmh.description: Heavy rail line speed in the reconstructed pre-2014 era. No 2014 public timetable has been obtained to validate this (DECISIONS.md 13 priority 8).

A.transit.era1_station_dwell_s.description: Heavy rail station dwell in the reconstructed pre-2014 era.

A.transit.s0_join_tolerance_m.description: Tolerance for joining the retained heavy rail alignment to the observed network in S0.

A.transit.sbc_extension_km.description: Broadmeadow extension length as STATED in the Strategic Business Case. The alignment routed over observed OSM centreline is 7.00 km, 5.3% longer. The model uses the routed geometry; this field records the published figure.

A.parking.capacity_default.description: Fallback capacity where a parking facility carries none. 4,861 of 7,710 facilities carry an observed capacity.

A.parking.free_occupancy_profile.description: Hourly occupancy profile for free parking. Assumed: parking meter transactions were not obtained (DECISIONS.md 13 priority 6-adjacent).

A.active.footway_width_default.description: Fallback footway width. Footway widths were not obtained for Newcastle.

held_fixed.rule: A data-join tolerance, not a model parameter. It decides which observed TfNSW signal is the same physical intersection as a clustered OSM one, and no behaviour, run time or score reads it - only the identity written into scats_site_id. It is held fixed rather than swept because a sweep could not change the join: all 14 corridor intersections match inside 26 m, so every radius from the 45 m OSM clustering distance up to about 100 m yields the identical assignment, and widening it past that would begin attaching an intersection to its neighbour rather than resolving a real ambiguity. Declaring a sweep interval over which the output is constant would be the defect this project has already hit three times.
held_fixed.departure_requires: a re-measured match-distance distribution showing a corridor intersection falling outside this radius, or a corridor extension into an area where signals sit closer together than the radius

A.signals.scats_match_radius_m.description: Radius within which an intersection in A2_signal_control_corridor.csv is matched to a signal in the TfNSW Traffic Lights Location inventory, to recover its SCATS site number and installation date. The corridor intersections are clusters of OSM traffic-signal nodes and carry no identifier of their own; the TfNSW inventory is the only observed source of both. Measured match distances on the 14 corridor intersections range from 1 to 26 m.
